text: A deterrent is something that makes people afraid to do a bad thing, so they decide not to. Here, strong submarines would make other countries think twice before attacking Australia.
Sceptical means not sure that something is true or a good idea, and wanting more proof first. Americans usually spell it skeptical.
To revamp something is to change it a lot so it is newer or works better. America and Britain changed many laws so they could share secret technology.
A seahorse is a small fish with a head shaped like a horse's. It is a weak swimmer and likes to hold on to things with its tail.
Bony fish are fish with skeletons made of hard bone, which is true of most fish you know. Sharks are the famous exception, since theirs is softer cartilage.
An artefact is an object made by people. Here, piers and docks are human artefacts that seahorses hold on to. Americans spell it artifact.
A pier is a long platform that sticks out from the shore over the water, where boats can tie up.
Rebar is short for reinforcing bar, a steel rod used to make concrete stronger. Here the divers used grids of it as a new home for the seahorses.
A naval base is a port where a navy keeps its ships and submarines, repairs them, and houses its sailors.
A nuclear-powered ship runs on heat from a small nuclear reactor instead of burning fuel. This is different from carrying nuclear weapons.
An attack submarine is built to hunt other ships and submarines. It is not the kind that carries long-range nuclear missiles.
Careful: here project means to send out or show, not a school project. A base that projects power lets a country show its strength far from home.
Conventional means ordinary or traditional. Conventional missiles use regular explosives, not nuclear ones.
Land-based means launched from the ground rather than from a ship or plane.
Guam is a small island in the western Pacific Ocean that belongs to the United States and has an American military base.
AUKUS is a deal among Australia, the UK and the US, named for their first letters. The three countries agreed to work together on submarines and other technology.
Jointly means together, as a team, instead of one at a time.
Virginia-class is a type of American nuclear-powered attack submarine. Each one is named for a class, like a model of car.
Here sail means to operate a vessel, even a submarine that goes underwater and has no sails at all.
To deploy is to send people or equipment somewhere to do a job, like soldiers going on a mission.
A workover is a round of repairs and upgrades on a ship or machine.
A phase is one step or stage in a plan that happens over time.
Diesel is a fuel used in trucks and some boats. A diesel submarine must come up to the surface often to get air for its engines.
Here surfacing means coming up from underwater to the top of the ocean.
Potent means strong and powerful.
Here range is a verb: to travel over a wide area. Subs that range far can go to faraway places.
Something controversial is something people argue about because they strongly disagree.
To negotiate is to talk through a deal until everyone agrees. Here the three countries worked out AUKUS mostly in secret.
Careful: here row rhymes with cow and means a loud argument, not a line of seats.
A plotter is someone who makes a secret plan. Here it is a joking word for the leaders who made the AUKUS deal.
Overwhelming means so big or so much that it is hard to handle.
Creaky usually describes an old squeaky door. Here it means old and worn out, and not working well.
A shipyard is a place where ships and submarines are built or repaired.
A jab is a quick poke or punch. A big jab of cash means a sudden, large amount of money pushed in, like a booster shot.
To pledge is to promise to give something. Australia promised to give 6.2 billion dollars and has paid part of it.
A think-tank is a group of experts who study problems, such as politics, and share their ideas.
A drop in the bucket means a tiny amount compared with how much is needed, like one cup of water for a swimming pool.
A transactional person treats relationships like trades, asking what they get in return for each deal.
Full speed ahead is a ship captain's order to go as fast as possible. It means to go forward with no slowing down.
An infusion is something poured in, like money added to help a project.
To jolt is to give a sudden shake or shock, here to wake the industry up.
Torpor is a sleepy, slow state when nothing much gets done, like a bear's winter nap.
A slew of means a large number of something.
A sanctum is a very private, special place. The innermost sanctum means the most trusted circle.
Hypersonic means moving at more than five times the speed of sound.
Quantum computing is a new kind of computer that uses the strange rules of tiny particles to solve some problems very fast.
Classified means officially secret, so only people with permission can see it.
Hypothetical means imagined, not real, like asking what would happen if something occurred.
Here rotate means to take turns being in a place. The submarines come and go in turns rather than staying forever.
Sleight of hand is a magician's trick that fools your eyes. Here it means a way of describing something that hides the real situation.
A commodore is a navy officer who leads a group of ships or submarines.
A meltdown is when a nuclear reactor gets so hot that it is badly damaged. Backup power keeps the cooling systems working.
Auxiliary means extra or backup, there to help the main system.
The seabed is the floor of the ocean.
Tax-free means you do not have to pay the usual tax on what you buy.
Here an oval is a big oval-shaped field for playing sports like cricket.
Cricket is a bat-and-ball sport, popular in Australia, Britain and India, a bit like baseball.
To persist is to keep going or stay, even when you would like it to stop.
A ship that is Australian-flagged belongs to Australia and flies its flag.
